subject: Cloud Computing
title: FinOps: Making Cloud Costs Visible
description: One-minute skill: FinOps: Making Cloud Costs Visible.

hook.text: Cloud bills are out of control. FinOps brings finance, engineering, and business together to manage cloud spending.

buildup.text: Engineers choose resources, finance pays the bill, and nobody has shared visibility. FinOps fixes this disconnect.

discovery.text: FinOps tools show exactly which team, project, and feature costs what. Cost becomes a metric, just like performance.

twist.text: The FinOps Foundation reports most companies waste 30% of cloud spend. Visibility alone can cut costs dramatically.

climax.text: FinOps is now a career path. The FinOps Foundation certifies practitioners and publishes cloud cost best practices.

punchline.text: 30% of cloud spending is waste. FinOps makes it visible to cut it.

quiz.question: What fundamental problem does FinOps address?
options: The disconnect between engineering resource choices and financial accountability
The need to eliminate all cloud spending
The requirement for engineers to learn accounting

details.summary: FinOps is a practice that brings financial accountability to cloud spending by combining engineering, finance, and business teams to optimize costs. It treats cloud spending as a variable operating expense that requires continuous monitoring, optimization, and governance.
details.whyItMatters: Cloud spending grows faster than most organizations expect. FinOps practices prevent waste, improve forecasting, and ensure that cloud investments deliver measurable business value.
takeaways: FinOps combines engineering and finance for cloud cost management
Typical organizations waste 20 to 30 percent of cloud spending

faq.question: What are the main FinOps practices?
faq.answer: Tagging all resources for cost attribution, regularly right-sizing instances, using reserved and spot instances strategically, setting budgets and alerts, reviewing spending weekly, and empowering engineering teams with cost visibility and accountability for their spending.

faq.question: How much can FinOps save?
faq.answer: Organizations typically find 20 to 40 percent savings through FinOps practices. Common wins include terminating idle resources, right-sizing over-provisioned instances, purchasing reservations for stable workloads, and moving infrequently accessed data to cheaper storage tiers.
